findings.claim: Removing the `isWithinPath` helper will break compilation if the `declarations.every(...)` callback below still references it.
findings.rationale: The hunk deletes the helper but the visible tail of the function (`declarations.every((declaration) => {`) is unchanged in this hunk, and that callback was the only plausible consumer of `isWithinPath`. Unless a separate hunk rewrites the callback body, this leaves an unresolved identifier (TS2304). Medium-high confidence that the callback must also change; I can't see it here to confirm.

findings.claim: Dropping the `workspaceRoot` check changes which declarations are classified as external node_modules, likely suppressing JSDoc for workspace-internal/linked packages.
findings.rationale: The previous logic combined `process.cwd()` with `isWithinPath` so that declarations inside the workspace (e.g. symlinked monorepo packages resolved through a local `node_modules`, or `node_modules` nested inside the repo) were not treated as external. Without it, any path containing `node_modules` is presumably treated as external, so JSDoc comments from sibling workspace packages would now be omitted from the generated OpenAPI output. This is a silent behavior change for existing callers; moderate confidence since the predicate body isn't shown.

findings.claim: `normalize` may become an unused local after `workspaceRoot` is deleted.
findings.rationale: `workspaceRoot` was one of the two call sites of `normalize`. If the remaining `declarations.every` callback no longer normalizes declaration file names (which it must do if the workspace comparison is gone), `normalize` becomes dead code and will trip `noUnusedLocals`/lint. Low-to-medium confidence; it's likely still used to normalize `declaration.getSourceFile().fileName` before the `node_modules` check.
